180: static int sdio_wait_command(struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv, uint32_t cmd)
181: {
182:   clock_t deadline = clock_systime_ticks() + MSEC2TICK(1000);
183:   uint32_t status;
184: 
185:   for (;;)
186:     {
187:       status = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS);
188:       if ((status & (BK7258_SDIO_CMD_NO_RESPONSE |
189:                      BK7258_SDIO_CMD_RESPONSE_END |
190:                      BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT)) != 0)
191:         {
192:           break;
193:         }
194: 
195:       if ((int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - deadline) >= 0)
196:         {
197:           printf("SDIO CMD%u timeout status=0x%08lx\n",
198:                  (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
199:                  (unsigned long)status);
200:           return -ETIMEDOUT;
201:         }
202: 
203:       /* At transfer speed the RX FIFO can fill before a 100 us sleep
204:        * expires.  Keep the PIO loop tight while data is active; otherwise a
205:        * 512-byte sector consistently overflows after the first 256 bytes. */
206:       if (!priv->data_active)
207:         {
208:           nxsig_usleep(100);
209:         }
210:     }
211: 
212:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS,
213:              status & (BK7258_SDIO_CMD_NO_RESPONSE |
214:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_RESPONSE_END |
215:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT |
216:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_OK |
217:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_FAIL));
218: 
219:   if ((status & BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT) != 0)
220:     {
221:       printf("SDIO CMD%u response timeout status=0x%08lx\n",
222:              (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
223:              (unsigned long)status);
224:       return -ETIMEDOUT;
225:     }
226: 
227:   /* The BK7258 host reports CRC failure for the open-drain/long-response
228:    * identification commands even when the vendor stack accepts the response.
229:    * Armino explicitly tolerates this for ACMD41, CMD2 and CMD9.  Keep the
230:    * same compatibility rule while preserving CRC errors for normal R1/R7.
231:    */
232:   if ((status & BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_FAIL) != 0 &&
233:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != SD_ACMDIDX41 &&
234:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX2 &&
235:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX9)
236:     {
237:       printf("SDIO CMD%u CRC error status=0x%08lx\n",
238:              (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
239:              (unsigned long)status);
240:       return -EIO;
241:     }
242: 
243:   return OK;
244: }

667: /****************************************************************************
668:  * Name: SDIO_WAITRESPONSE
669:  *
670:  * Description:
671:  *   Poll-wait for the response to the last command to be ready.  This
672:  *   function should be called even after sending commands that have no
673:  *   response (such as CMD0) to make sure that the hardware is ready to
674:  *   receive the next command.
675:  *
676:  * Input Parameters:
677:  *   dev  - An instance of the SDIO device interface
678:  *   cmd  - The command that was sent.  See 32-bit command definitions above.
679:  *
680:  * Returned Value:
681:  *   OK is success; a negated errno on failure
682:  *
683:  ****************************************************************************/
684: 
685: #define SDIO_WAITRESPONSE(dev,cmd) ((dev)->waitresponse(dev,cmd))

688:  * Name: SDIO_RECVRx
689:  *
690:  * Description:
691:  *   Receive response to SDIO command.  Only the critical payload is
692:  *   returned -- that is 32 bits for 48 bit status and 128 bits for 136 bit
693:  *   status.  The driver implementation should verify the correctness of
694:  *   the remaining, non-returned bits (CRCs, CMD index, etc.).
695:  *
696:  * Input Parameters:
697:  *   dev    - An instance of the SDIO device interface
698:  *   Rx - Buffer in which to receive the response
699:  *
700:  * Returned Value:

702:  *   failure means only a faiure to obtain the requested response (due to
703:  *   transport problem -- timeout, CRC, etc.).  The implementation only
704:  *   assures that the response is returned intacta and does not check errors
705:  *   within the response itself.
706:  *
707:  ****************************************************************************/

717: /****************************************************************************
718:  * Name: SDIO_WAITENABLE
719:  *
720:  * Description:
721:  *   Enable/disable of a set of SDIO wait events.  This is part of the
722:  *   the SDIO_WAITEVENT sequence.  The set of to-be-waited-for events is
723:  *   configured before calling either calling SDIO_DMARECVSETUP,
724:  *   SDIO_DMASENDSETUP, or SDIO_WAITEVENT.  This is the recommended
725:  *   ordering:
726:  *
727:  *     SDIO_WAITENABLE:    Discard any pending interrupts, enable event(s)
728:  *                         of interest
729:  *     SDIO_DMARECVSETUP/
730:  *     SDIO_DMASENDSETUP:  Setup the logic that will trigger the event the
731:  *                         event(s) of interest
732:  *     SDIO_WAITEVENT:     Wait for the event of interest (which might
733:  *                         already have occurred)
734:  *
735:  *   This sequence should eliminate race conditions between the command/
736:  *   transfer setup and the subsequent events.
737:  *
738:  *   The enabled events persist until either (1) SDIO_WAITENABLE is called
739:  *   again specifying a different set of wait events, or (2) SDIO_EVENTWAIT
740:  *   returns.
741:  *
742:  * Input Parameters:
743:  *   dev      - An instance of the SDIO device interface
744:  *   eventset - A bitset of events to enable or disable (see SDIOWAIT_*
745:  *              definitions). 0=disable; 1=enable.
746:  *   timeout  - Maximum time in milliseconds to wait.  Zero means immediate
747:  *              timeout with no wait.  The timeout value is ignored if
748:  *              SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT is not included in the waited-for eventset.
749:  *
750:  * Returned Value:
751:  *   None
752:  *
753:  ****************************************************************************/
754: 
755: #define SDIO_WAITENABLE(dev,eventset,timeout) ((dev)->waitenable(dev,eventset,timeout))

803:  *
804:  * Description:
805:  *   Register a callback that that will be invoked on any media status
806:  *   change.  Callbacks should not be made from interrupt handlers, rather
807:  *   interrupt level events should be handled by calling back on the work
808:  *   thread.
809:  *

**Findings**

1. **High: Normal 512-byte reads no longer use the BK7258 vendor-required multi-block receive mode.**  
   [bk7258_sdio.c:490](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:490), `sdio_recvsetup()`

   The diff changes the condition for `BK7258_SDIO_DATA_MULTIBLOCK` from `blocklen == 512` to `nblocks > 1`. The active configuration sets `CONFIG_MMCSD_MULTIBLOCK_LIMIT=1`, so every filesystem sector read now clears this bit.

   This regresses from the vendor V2 implementation, which unconditionally calls `sdio_host_hal_set_read_multi_block_data()` for reads at [sdio_host_driver.c:790](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:790). The vendor’s single-block path still uses that setup before issuing CMD17 at [sd_card_driver.c:1695](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:1695). Therefore this is not simply CMD17 versus CMD18 semantics; it is a BK7258 data-engine workaround expected even for a one-sector request. Probe may succeed because SCR is only eight bytes, while subsequent MBR/filesystem reads fail or complete incorrectly.

   Minimal fix: restore the 512-byte condition for this fixed SD-NAND path, while keeping short transfers such as SCR in single-block mode.

2. **High: RX FIFO overflow is enabled as a terminal IRQ even though FIFO data is not drained until transfer completion.**  
   [bk7258_sdio.c:143](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:143), `sdio_interrupt()`  
   [bk7258_sdio.c:502](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:502), `sdio_recvsetup()`  
   [bk7258_sdio.c:605](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:605), `sdio_eventwait()`

   The new mask enables `BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_OVERFLOW`. When it fires, the ISR immediately sets `data_result = -EIO`, clears `data_active`, and wakes the waiter. `sdio_eventwait()` then takes the error branch without draining any FIFO data and resets the receive state.

   This conflicts with the controller’s completion-only PIO model, where the FIFO may fill and gate the SD clock before task-context draining. The vendor default mask explicitly excludes RX overflow at [sdio_ll.h:445](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/middleware/soc/bk7258/hal/sdio_ll.h:445), and its V2 RX ISR intentionally leaves overflow out of the receive condition at [sdio_host_driver.c:1341](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:1341). Enabling it here can convert the expected full-FIFO condition into an early failed transfer.

   Minimal fix: follow the vendor path by not enabling or treating RX overflow as terminal for completion-only PIO. Supporting it correctly would instead require servicing `RX_NEED_READ` and draining incrementally before the FIFO fills.

3. **Medium: Media callback registration claims success but callbacks are never invoked, preventing recovery after an initial probe failure.**  
   [bk7258_sdio.c:638](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:638), `sdio_callbackenable()`  
   [bk7258_sdio.c:651](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:651), `sdio_registercallback()`  
   [bk7258_mmcsd.c:50](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:50), `bk7258_mmcsd_initialize()`

   The lower half stores the callback, argument, and event mask but contains no path that calls or queues the callback. When initial probing fails, NuttX deliberately enables `SDIOMEDIA_INSERTED` at [mmcsd_sdio.c:4611](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:4611). Since this driver always reports `SDIO_STATUS_PRESENT`, `callbackenable()` should immediately perform the one-shot inserted callback, as established lower halves do at [stm32_sdio.c:2642](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/stm32/stm32_sdio.c:2642).

   With the fallback block driver removed, a transient boot-time probe failure now leaves `/dev/mmcsd0` absent until reboot despite the MMCSD core arming a retry callback.

   Minimal fix: when callbacks are enabled, compare the requested media event with `sdio_status()`, clear the one-shot event mask, and call the registered callback directly in task context or queue it on `HPWORK` from interrupt context. A bounded board-level reprobe is another viable fix.
